name: Heart attack
tagline: Chest pain that doesn't pass — call now.

urgent.heading: Urgent — call now
urgent.primary_message: Call an ambulance immediately. Chew one aspirin if available. Do not drive yourself.
red_flags: Chest pain, pressure, tightness, or squeezing — lasting more than a few minutes
Pain spreading to the arm (often left), jaw, neck, back, or stomach
Sudden shortness of breath, with or without chest pain
Sudden severe weakness, dizziness, or fainting
In women: unusual fatigue, indigestion-like pain, or back pain

what_is_it.heading: Heart attack in plain terms
what_is_it.lede: A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is suddenly blocked. The muscle starts dying within minutes.
paragraphs: Most heart attacks are caused by a clot forming on a fatty plaque inside a coronary artery. The blockage starves the heart muscle of oxygen. The longer the artery stays blocked, the more muscle dies.
Modern hospital treatment can open the blocked artery and save the rest of the heart — but only if you get there fast. Every minute of delay is more permanent damage.

items.headline: Time = muscle
items.body: Every minute of blocked artery is more heart muscle lost. Treatment in the first hours can save most of it.

items.headline: Leading killer
items.body: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of non-communicable death in South Africa.

items.headline: Atypical in women
items.body: Women often have less classic chest pain — instead, fatigue, jaw pain, nausea, or shortness of breath. These signs are easy to dismiss.

items.headline: Largely preventable
items.body: Smoking, high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, inactivity, and obesity drive most heart attacks. All are manageable.

pull_quote.text: Most people who die of a heart attack die before they reach hospital — usually because they waited, hoping it would pass. If you are not sure, call.

signs.heading: What you might feel
signs.lede: Heart attack symptoms are not always dramatic. Mild but persistent symptoms still need urgent attention.

items.title: Chest pain or pressure
items.description: A heavy, squeezing, tight, or burning feeling in the centre of the chest. Lasts more than a few minutes, or comes and goes.

items.title: Pain spreading outwards
items.description: Pain or numbness in the arm (often left), jaw, neck, back, or upper stomach. Can occur without chest pain.

items.title: Shortness of breath
items.description: Sudden difficulty breathing, sometimes the only sign. More common in women, older adults, and people with diabetes.

items.title: Sweating, nausea, dizziness
items.description: Cold clammy sweat, nausea or vomiting, sudden weakness or fainting. Often combined with the symptoms above.

myths.heading: What is true and what is not

items.myth: A heart attack always means dramatic chest pain.
items.fact: Many heart attacks start with mild discomfort and build slowly. Women, older adults, and people with diabetes often have atypical symptoms.

items.myth: If I'm young and fit, I can't have a heart attack.
items.fact: Heart attacks in young South Africans are increasing — driven by smoking, vaping, drug use, family history, and undiagnosed cholesterol problems.

items.myth: Indigestion that won't go away is just indigestion.
items.fact: Heartburn-like pain that lasts, returns, comes with sweating or shortness of breath, or feels different from normal — must be checked out.

items.myth: I'll wait an hour to see if it passes.
items.fact: Waiting is the single biggest reason people die of heart attacks. If you are unsure for more than 10 minutes — call the ambulance.

action_steps.heading: What to do — the moment you suspect a heart attack

items.title: Call 10177 or 112 immediately
items.description: Say 'suspected heart attack'. Paramedics start treatment in the ambulance and route to a cardiac-capable hospital.

items.title: Chew one regular aspirin (300 mg) if available
items.description: Chewing — not swallowing whole — gets aspirin into the blood faster. Skip if allergic, on blood thinners, or recently had bleeding.

items.title: Sit down and rest. Loosen tight clothing
items.description: Sit comfortably. Do not lie flat if breathing is difficult. Stay calm — panic increases the strain on the heart.

items.title: Do not drive yourself
items.description: If you collapse at the wheel, you could die and harm others. Wait for the ambulance — paramedics carry life-saving equipment.

items.title: Unlock the door for paramedics
items.description: Make sure they can reach you fast. If alone, get to a place where someone can find you.

get_help.heading: Who to call right now
get_help.lede: Suspected heart attack is an emergency. Do not wait, do not drive, do not 'see how it goes'.

helplines.name: Emergency (mobile)
helplines.description: Reaches any emergency service from a cellphone
